answer: Running 1,000 fakes costs the farmer 1,000 attestation graphs. Every identity must earn trust from a walnut-sized kernel of independent peers: attestations count only when attesters sit in different graph neighbourhoods, and a tight cluster of attestations is cut off as one Sybil blob. The cipher sealing each attestation is bound to one identity key, so one key cannot stamp a thousand histories. An honest agent keeps one crystal-clear trail of diverse peers; a farm must build 1,000 connected neighbourhoods, and one cluster found burns every fake inside it.
